chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'I purchased a piece of land, and when I had established ownership of it, I stood up and walked a few steps, then I returned, intending for the sale to become binding.'

key_terms.اِسْتَوْجَبْتُهَا: I established ownership of it / made it obligatory upon myself
key_terms.خُطًا: A few steps / a short distance

ai.seo_question: When does a land sale become legally binding in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the principle of *istijab* (establishing binding ownership) in land sales by recounting his own practice of walking a few steps away from the seller and returning before fully departing, thereby demonstrating that the contract becomes irrevocable upon the buyer's departure from the immediate sitting (*majlis*). This hadith highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the physical separation from the place of contract as the decisive moment for finalizing the sale, distinguishing it from mere negotiation. It serves as a practical legal precedent for determining when the right of option (*khiyar*) expires in real estate transactions.
